Lena Varga-Holm
Senior Data Engineer | Data Platform
Email: [EMAIL] | Phone: [PHONE] | LinkedIn: [LINK]

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Senior Data Engineer with experience owning ingestion and orchestration for a data platform built on Airflow, Snowflake, dbt and Kafka. Designed and operated production data pipelines processing around 30 million events per day, with end-to-end latency under two minutes at p95. Delivered measurable improvements in warehouse build time, database load and cloud warehouse costs. Experienced in Python, SQL, data quality, open-source contributions and mentoring engineers.

EXPERIENCE

Senior Data Engineer | Lukovac Freight Hub d.o.o. | 2022–Present
- Own ingestion and orchestration for the data platform using Airflow, Snowflake, dbt and Kafka; participate in the data-platform on-call rotation one week in six.
- Designed and built a shipment-event streaming pipeline using partner webhooks, Kafka, Kafka Connect and Snowpipe Streaming, processing around 30 million events per day with end-to-end latency under two minutes at p95.
- Added a dead-letter topic and replay tooling so failed events can be reprocessed without data loss.
- Migrated approximately 300 stored procedures into dbt models with tests and documentation; introduced incremental models and slim CI using state:modified in GitHub Actions. Cut the nightly warehouse build from 5 hours 10 minutes to 1 hour 35 minutes and made lineage visible to analysts.
- Replaced hourly full-table extracts from the orders database with Debezium change data capture into Kafka, reducing replica CPU during loads from around 70% to around 25%.
- Reduced the Snowflake bill from approximately $38,000 to $24,000 per month in 2024 through warehouse sizing, auto-suspend and removing unused tables.
- Mentor two mid-level engineers and run data platform office hours.

Data Engineer | Kovalent Pay | 2019–2022
- Built PySpark batch jobs on AWS EMR to match bank settlement files against internal ledgers for a transaction reconciliation engine.
- Reduced the finance team's manual reconciliation work from around three days to around four hours per month-end.
- Worked on Redshift warehouse design and data quality using Great Expectations.

OPEN-SOURCE CONTRIBUTIONS
- Fixed a pagination bug and added tests for a community Airflow provider package for a SaaS CRM API; two pull requests were merged. Technologies: Python, Airflow, pytest.

SKILLS
Python, SQL, PySpark, Airflow, dbt, Kafka, Kafka Connect, Debezium, Snowflake, AWS MSK, AWS EMR, S3, Glue Data Catalog, Redshift, PostgreSQL, Terraform, GitHub Actions, Great Expectations, pytest, data ingestion and orchestration, streaming pipelines, change data capture, data quality, warehouse optimisation.

CERTIFICATION
AWS Certified Data Engineer – Associate | May 2024

EDUCATION
MSc in Computer Science | Northgate Technical University
Thesis: Incremental materialized views
docs.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform role at Halden Pay. My experience combines production data-platform ownership with payment-data engineering, including building reliable pipelines and improving the operational performance of the systems teams depend on.

At Lukovac Freight Hub, I own ingestion and orchestration across Airflow, Snowflake, dbt and Kafka. I designed a shipment-event pipeline processing around 30 million events per day at under two minutes' end-to-end latency at p95, and added dead-letter and replay tooling to support recovery without data loss. I also migrated approximately 300 stored procedures to tested and documented dbt models, cutting the nightly warehouse build from 5 hours 10 minutes to 1 hour 35 minutes. These projects reflect the reusable, well-operated platform approach described in your role.

Earlier, at Kovalent Pay, I built PySpark reconciliation jobs that matched bank settlement files against internal ledgers and reduced manual month-end work for finance from around three days to around four hours. I have also reduced Snowflake costs through warehouse optimisation, contributed fixes and tests to an open-source Airflow provider, and currently mentor two engineers. I would bring this combination of platform ownership, data quality, operational care and payment-domain experience to Halden Pay's Data Platform team.

I am particularly interested in the team's focus on shared platform capabilities and reusable frameworks. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience could support the data platform and the teams that rely on it.

Kind regards,
Lena Varga-Holm
